claims_about_contribution.why: Merely asserts contribution.md exists alongside other submission files in submission/; consistent with contribution.md being the document under review there. No content of contribution.md is misdescribed by this statement.

differences.user_quote: The canonical existing method (Raman 2026's white-bear steering, in `papers/`) contrasts **"think about X" vs "don't think about X"** from WorkspaceBench's `directed_modulation` bank.
differences.judge_quote: Origin: contrastive activation addition, referenced to un-instructed production instead of an opposite instruction.

differences.user_quote: the paper's secondary "hold vs mention" contrast failed; the paper never tested a bare-copy reference

differences.what: Explicit statement that the prompt source (self-authored pairs) differs from the paper's dataset (directed_modulation bank), naming that bank
differences.user_quote: self-authored prompt pairs (28 fresh concept/sentence pairs) rather than the `directed_modulation` items, which the WBS paper explicitly restricted itself to.
differences.judge_quote:
28 prompts that
instruct the model to "think about X while you write" a sentence, and 28 prompts that instruct it
only to write the same sentence

rationale: The judge is given only a generic, unnamed lineage ("contrastive activation addition, referenced to un-instructed production instead of an opposite instruction") with no mention of any specific paper, benchmark, or named prior method. The user, by contrast, is explicitly told the planted prior work's name (Raman 2026, "white-bear steering"), its file location, its benchmark source (WorkspaceBench's directed_modulation bank), and a point-by-point comparison (including that the paper's own secondary ablation failed) arguing why the submitted method is not a reproduction — strictly more identifying and overlap/novelty detail than contribution.md discloses.
